name: Hotel de Crillon
insider_take: Arguably Paris's most storied address, the Hôtel de Crillon sits on the Place de la Concorde in an 18th-century palace built by order of King Louis XV — where history, haute couture, and Rosewood's signature soul converge in breathtaking fashion.
whats_special: Originally commissioned in 1758 by King Louis XV, the building has witnessed some of history's most pivotal moments — including the signing of the French-American Treaty of Alliance in 1778. Following a stunning four-year restoration by Karl Lagerfeld and Aline Asmar d'Amman, the Crillon reopened in 2017, blending imperial grandeur with contemporary French artistry. The iconic Les Ambassadeurs bar — with its soaring ceilings and marble columns — is one of the most glamorous cocktail destinations in all of Europe. Guests enjoy unrivaled views over the Place de la Concorde, with the Eiffel Tower and the Tuileries Garden as a backdrop.
pro_tip: Book a room or suite on the Place de la Concorde side — waking up to that view is a once-in-a-lifetime Parisian moment. For the ultimate treat, reserve the Blossom suite, personally designed by Karl Lagerfeld himself.
dont_miss: L'Écrin Restaurant: Chef Boris Campanella's intimate fine-dining jewel box — one of Paris's most beautifully designed dining rooms. The Crillon Rose Spa: An underground sanctuary offering bespoke treatments inspired by the iconic Crillon Rose. Place de la Concorde: Step outside and stand at the very heart of Parisian history — the Champs-Élysées, the Louvre, and the Musée d'Orsay are all within easy walking distance.
pros: Iconic palace hotel on Place de la Concorde with rich French heritage
Exquisite Rosewood renovation blending historic grandeur with modern luxury
Prime central Paris location near major attractions and shopping
World-class dining experiences and exceptional personalized service
cons: Ultra-luxury pricing reflecting palace hotel status
Formal atmosphere may not suit all travelers
